1976.notes: ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1976-77 ed. Vol. II, Table 106 (State Individual Income Taxes: Rates, July 1, 1976), Table 107 (personal exemptions, July 1, 1976) and Table 108 (standard deduction, July 1, 1976). 1977.notes: P.L. 1975 c. 661 (36 M.R.S. §5111 as repealed and replaced): third rate table, 'for any taxable year or portion thereof on or after January 1, 1977' (1% to 10% on $2,000/$4,000/$6,000/$8,000/$10,000/$15,000/$25,000); matches the ACIR July 1976 note that rates from 1977 range from 1% to 10% over $25,000. P.L. 1977 c. 686 §7 inserted the next table effective July 1, 1978, so 1977 used this table all year. Joint returns: rates apply to income classes twice as large (ACIR July 1976 and July 1980 tables; joint schedule doubled accordingly). Deduction = $1,000 personal exemption per federal exemption (§5126; P.L. 1977 c. 686 §10 kept $1,000 except for 1978) and the §5124-A standard deduction enacted by P.L. 1977 c. 477 §17 (effective Oct. 24, 1977): the higher of a low-income allowance of $1,700 / $2,100 or 16% of Maine AGI up to $2,400 / $2,800. 1978 is not transcribed: two rate tables applied (prorated by days under §5234) and the 1978 exemption was conditionally $1,200.

1978.notes: Two statutory tables applied in 1978, blended by days: P.L. 1977 c. 686 s. 7 (Laws of Maine scan) inserted into 36 M.R.S. s. 5111 a table 'for any taxable year or portion thereof on or after July 1, 1978' (1%, 2%, 3%, 6%, 7%, 8%, 9.2%, 10% on $2,000/$4,000/$6,000/$8,000/$10,000/$15,000/$25,000), replacing the P.L. 1975 c. 661 table in force from January 1, 1977 (same brackets; 4% on $4,000-$6,000 and 9% on $15,000-$25,000). Under s. 5234 (enacted by P.L. 1975 c. 660 s. 9: when a rate changes during a taxable year the tax is the tax for the whole year at the old rate times the proportion of the year, in days, at the old rate plus the tax at the new rate times the proportion at the new rate) a calendar-year 1978 taxpayer owed 181/365 of the tax under the first table plus 184/365 under the second, which with identical brackets equals this schedule: the two brackets whose rate changed are recorded at the day-weighted rates (181 x 4% + 184 x 3%)/365 = 3.4959% and (181 x 9% + 184 x 9.2%)/365 = 9.1008%; the other rates were the same in both tables. The s. 5111 history on legislature.maine.gov lists no other amendment between P.L. 1975 c. 661 and I.B. 1981 c. 2. Joint returns: rates apply to income classes twice as large (ACIR July 1976 and July 1980 tables; joint schedule doubled accordingly). Deduction = $1,200 personal exemption per federal exemption for a taxable year ending during 1978 (s. 5126 as amended by P.L. 1977 c. 686 s. 10, conditional on first-half FY 1978-79 General Fund revenues meeting the revised estimates; P.L. 1979 c. 615 s. 4, https://lldc.mainelegislature.org/Open/Laws/1979/1979_PL_c615.pdf, re-enacted the $1,200 for a taxable year ending on or after December 31, 1978 and on or before November 30, 1979, for one taxable year only) and the s. 5124-A standard deduction enacted by P.L. 1977 c. 477 s. 17 (next amended by I.B. 1981 c. 2): the higher of a low-income allowance of $1,700 / $2,100 or 16% of Maine AGI up to $2,400 / $2,800. Maine did not index its brackets before 1982.

2023.notes: The standard deduction ($13,850 / $27,700) and exemption ($4,700 each) phase out with income, so they are left out.

2024.notes: The standard deduction ($14,600 / $29,200) and exemption ($5,000 each) phase out with income.

2025.notes: Maine did not adopt the One Big Beautiful Bill Act deduction for 2025: its standard deduction ($15,000 / $30,000) and exemption ($5,150 each) phase out with income.

2026.notes: Top bracket folds in the new 2% surcharge over $1M / $1.5M. The standard deduction ($15,700 / $31,400) and exemption ($5,300 each) phase out with income.
